nodes.summary: Bisimilar processes have the same immediate free-channel barbs.
nodes.title: Barbed bisimilar processes have the same barbs

nodes.summary: Structural congruence preserves immediate barbs.
nodes.title: Structural congruence preserves immediate barbs

nodes.summary: Waiting inputs are observable, despite being unable to reduce alone.
nodes.title: Barbs of an input prefix

nodes.summary: The inactive process has no barb, even after structural rearrangement.
nodes.title: The inactive process has no barbs

nodes.summary: A restricted output is visible exactly when its subject is free. Sending the private name on a free subject remains observable.
nodes.title: Barbs of a restricted output prefix

nodes.summary: Output readiness sees only its free subject and direction, not its object or guarded continuation.
nodes.title: Barbs of an output prefix

nodes.summary: Immediate free-channel readiness, up to the existing structural congruence. A witness performs no `Step`.
nodes.title: Immediate free-channel barb

nodes.summary: Every structural law of `Basic` is sound for strong barbed bisimilarity, including scope extrusion and replication unfolding.
nodes.title: Structurally congruent processes are barbed bisimilar

nodes.summary: Strong barbed bisimilarity, using the canonical CSLib bisimulation API. No context closure is built into this relation.
nodes.title: Strong barbed bisimilarity

nodes.summary: Labels for reductions and observation-only self-loops.
nodes.title: Labels for reductions and barb observations

nodes.summary: Structural congruence is a strong barbed bisimulation: reductions match one for one, while free-channel observations match immediately.
nodes.title: Structural congruence is a strong barbed bisimulation

nodes.summary: Every reduction needs an unguarded output in its source, even when communication is private or structural congruence is used arbitrarily.
nodes.title: Every reduction source has an unguarded output

nodes.summary: Structural rearrangement cannot expose an output from an input-guarded process. This includes arbitrary uses of replication and scope laws.
nodes.title: Structural congruence preserves unguarded outputs

nodes.summary: An output not behind a prefix, on any subject (including bound names). This is an overapproximation for arbitrary unguarded sums, not a barb.
nodes.title: Unguarded output in a process

nodes.summary: Waiting for input is not equivalent to doing nothing. Reduction-only bisimilarity would miss this distinction.
nodes.title: Free-channel input is not barbed bisimilar to nil

nodes.summary: The decorated LTS has precisely the strong reduction-matching and immediate-barb-preservation clauses of a strong barbed bisimulation.
nodes.title: Decorated-LTS bisimulations are exactly strong barbed bisimulations

nodes.summary: Strong barbed bisimilarity preserves finite may observations.
nodes.title: Barbed bisimilarity preserves may-barbs

nodes.summary: A free-channel barb reachable by finitely many existing reductions, possibly zero. This is a may observation, not a weak equivalence.
nodes.title: May-barb after finitely many reductions

nodes.summary: Outputless processes cannot reduce. Input guards may still have observable input barbs; this theorem does not identify them with `nil`.
nodes.title: Processes without unguarded output cannot reduce

nodes.summary: A visible input or output subject. Restricted variables are not subjects of these free-channel observations.
nodes.title: Free-channel input and output observables

nodes.summary: The existing reduction semantics decorated with barb tests. The observation transitions do not consume a prefix or transmit a name.
nodes.title: Reduction LTS decorated with barb observations

nodes.summary: A directly exposed guard is a barb, with the reflexive structural representative as witness.
nodes.title: Exposed guards are barbs

nodes.summary: A selected free-channel guard exposed without reduction. Restrictions hide bound subjects but do not hide free constants.
nodes.title: Free-channel guard offered without reduction

nodes.summary: A finite reduction path transfers across strong barbed bisimilarity.
nodes.title: Barbed bisimilarity transfers finite reduction paths

nodes.summary: A reduction from the first process is matched by one reduction, with strong barbed bisimilar derivatives.
nodes.title: Barbed bisimilarity matches each reduction by one reduction

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
